steps.title: Draw a curve
steps.instruction: Make the edit shown below, then run the whole program.
steps.explain: circle(radius) puts the turtle on the edge of a circle. The radius is the distance from the center to the edge. A second input limits the turn in degrees.
steps.expected: The new curve, beginning at the turtle’s current position.
steps.question: How would circle(40, 180) differ from circle(40)?
steps.answer: It draws a half-circle. Without the second input, circle(40) draws a full circle.
steps.help: Check the changed lines first. Keep parentheses and commas in place. Indent each line inside a loop or function by four spaces.

steps.title: Finish one connected line
steps.instruction: Make the edit shown below, then run the whole program.
steps.explain: goto(x, y) chooses a position: x moves left or right; y moves up or down. penup() lets you reposition without a connecting line. pendown() draws the next movement.
steps.expected: One complete connected line. Check it before making this code reusable.
steps.question: What happens if you leave the pen down while moving to a new starting point?
steps.answer: A connecting line appears between the previous position and the new one.

steps.title: Replace repetition with a loop
steps.instruction: Replace the repeated movement lines with the loop below. Run and compare.
steps.explain: The for line takes one item from the list at a time. The indented lines run for each item. The loop traces the same points you just wrote separately.
steps.expected: The same practice shape. The code now repeats the movement for you.
steps.question: Which line repeats? Which value changes on each repeat?
steps.answer: The indented drawing lines repeat. The loop variable takes the next value from the list each time.
steps.help: Check the changed lines first. Keep parentheses and commas in place. Indent each line inside a loop or function by four spaces.

steps.title: Name the connected line code
steps.instruction: Replace the tested example with this function and its call. Keep the call at the left edge.
steps.explain: def path(points, shade, width) names the code you tested. Its inputs replace the fixed values. The call underneath supplies those values and runs the indented body.
steps.expected: The practice shape should still appear. This step includes both the definition and a call.
steps.question: What would happen if you removed the path(...) call at the bottom?
steps.answer: The function would be stored, but this example would no longer draw. A definition only runs when it is called.
steps.help: End the def line with a colon. Indent the body four spaces and a nested loop another four spaces. Put the call at the left edge.

steps.title: Test one repeat
steps.instruction: Build one example using the value shown. Run and inspect it.
steps.explain: n has one value in this test. Follow how it controls the drawing before putting the commands in a loop.
steps.expected: One visible example from the group. Check its position, size, and color.
steps.question: Where is n used in the drawing code?
steps.answer: Find the variable in the movement, size, or color expressions. A different value changes those instructions.
